original_question: For the consumer-resource extensions in which consumers follow a dynamic cognitive map of resource locations, determine whether time-dependent solutions and spatially non-constant steady states exist in a bounded periodic domain with a top-hat detection kernel, and describe the qualitative properties of those steady states.
target_in_paper: Section 2.2.2, Open Problem 21, for the two new consumer-resource models (2.18) and (2.19).
correct_elements: Your draft correctly points to the consumer-resource part of the paper, identifies that the relevant extensions use a dynamic cognitive map of resource information, keeps the bounded-domain periodic setting and the top-hat detection kernel, and asks exactly about the three components that Open Problem 21 asks about: existence of time-dependent solutions, existence of spatially non-constant steady states, and the qualitative properties of those steady states.
missing_details: The paper's exact target is Open Problem 21, which is restricted to the two specific systems (2.18) and (2.19), not an arbitrary class of consumer-resource extensions.
The unknowns and their meanings should be made explicit: u(x,t) is the consumer density, v(x,t) is the resource density, and q(x,t) is the dynamic cognitive map.

The full PDEs should be stated: u_t = D1 Delta u - gamma div(u grad q_{g,R}) + c beta u v/(alpha+v) - d u, v_t = D2 Delta v + r v(1-v/K) - beta u v/(alpha+v), with q_t = b v - mu q in (2.18) and q_t = b u v - (mu + xi u) q in (2.19).
The nonlocal perception operator should be defined: q_{g,R}(x,t) = integral over Omega of q(y,t) g(x-y) dy, where g is the detection kernel and R is the perceptual radius.
The top-hat detection kernel should be specified as the one from (2.3): g(z) = 1/(2R) for |z| <= R and 0 otherwise in one dimension, with the higher-dimensional radial analogue allowed by the paper.
The parameter restrictions inherited from the surrounding context should be stated: D1, D2, gamma, c, beta, alpha, d, r, K, b > 0, mu >= 0, and xi >= 0 (xi appears only in (2.19)).
The boundary setting should be phrased exactly as a bounded domain with periodic boundary conditions; equivalently, the higher-dimensional periodic case can be viewed on a torus.

The paper asks 'in what sense do solutions exist', so the refined question should preserve that the solution concept and regularity class are part of the problem, rather than turning it into a bare yes/no existence question.
A qualitative comparison among the steady states of (2.14), (2.18), and (2.19) is a different nearby question, namely Open Problem 22, and should not be folded into this question.

No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restriction, or nilpotency condition is relevant here; the missing mathematical data are instead the PDE operators, the variables, the nonlocal kernel, the domain, and the parameter hypotheses.
refined_question:
For each of the two consumer-resource systems on a bounded domain Omega with periodic boundary conditions, where u(x,t) and v(x,t) denote the consumer and resource densities and q(x,t) is a dynamic cognitive map of previously found resources, namely
u_t = D1 Delta u - gamma div(u grad q_{g,R}) + c beta u v/(alpha+v) - d u,
v_t = D2 Delta v + r v(1-v/K) - beta u v/(alpha+v),
with either q_t = b v - mu q (model (2.18)) or q_t = b u v - (mu + xi u) q (model (2.19)), where q_{g,R}(x,t) = integral over Omega of q(y,t) g(x-y) dy and g is the top-hat detection kernel g(z)=1/(2R) for |z|<=R and 0 otherwise (or the corresponding radial top-hat kernel in higher dimensions), and with parameters D1, D2, gamma, c, beta, alpha, d, r, K, b > 0, mu >= 0, xi >= 0, in what solution sense do the time-dependent problems admit solutions for suitable initial data, do there exist spatially non-constant steady states, and what qualitative properties do such non-constant steady states possess?
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of Open Problem 21 in Sect. 2.2.2. The surrounding discussion first introduces the base consumer-resource model (2.14), then the two new dynamic-cognitive-map extensions (2.18) and (2.19), and finally asks, for the periodic bounded-domain problem with a top-hat detection function, in what sense time-dependent solutions exist, in what sense spatially non-constant steady states exist, and what qualitative properties those steady states have. The draft is close, but it should explicitly name the two exact systems, define the nonlocal operator q_{g,R} and the top-hat kernel, and preserve the paper's 'in what sense' wording; otherwise it risks drifting either to a broader class of extensions or to the separate comparison question in Open Problem 22.
